_comment: Transcribed from the two drawings in 'Jacket T&I Sequence': ST-CGF Jacket Launch Sequence (2021-4589-66-0007 Rev 1B1) and ST-CGF Jacket Floatation & Upending Installation Sequence (2021-4589-66-0009-01/-02 Rev 2). Used by data/3d-model/pipeline/build_ti_sequence.py. Brackets on the drawing (extreme of the COG / weight sensitivity runs) are kept in the *_extreme fields.

notes: Launching barge 142.5 m x 36 m x 8.5 m, mean draft 4.48 m before launch; vessel layout pending confirmation.
Design water depth for the bottom clearance during launch is 52.30 m (LAT); LAT is -2.80 m from MSL.
Results are for a dynamic friction of 0.05 and a winch speed of 0.30 m/s, from the ST-CGF launch analysis report 2021-4589-6K-1015_XA.
Jacket weight and COG are from the MOSES model; the Offshore Installation Contractor decides the final barge trim and draft for launch.

upending.drawing: ST-CGF Jacket Floatation & Upending Installation Sequence, 2021-4589-66-0009-01/-02 Rev 2 (TPGM 220480C-1100-DW-3601-7409)
notes: Elevations are from MSL; dimensions in mm unless stated. Mudline is at EL (-) 52.300 m and the water level at (-) 2.80 m LAT.
The upending sequence is based on a jacket weight of 5435 MT (factored, no sensitivity on COG); results for the weight and COG sensitivity cases are in brackets.
Four slings are used (rows A2, A5, C2 and C5). Internal compartment pressure is assumed to be 0.3 bar.
Controlled flooding is needed for the buoyancy tanks and legs; free flooding may be used for compartments that can be manually flooded and lie below the waterline.
The minimum required seabed clearance during upending is 2.1 m for all cases. The Offshore Installation Contractor develops the final upending sequences.
Results are from the jacket floatation & upending analysis report 2021-4589-6J-1016 Rev 2.

buoyancy_tanks.note: centre tank, not in the model

stages.name: Jacket free floating
actions: Jacket free floating with the lifting slings connected to the padeyes.

stages.name: Flood buoyancy tank BT-H0-C
actions: Commence controlled flooding of buoyancy tank BT-H0-C to 100%.

stages.name: Lift the hook to 42 m
actions: Lift the hook to a height of 42 m from the water surface.

stages.name: Flood buoyancy tanks BT-A2-1 and BT-A5-1 to 30%
actions: Maintain the hook at 42 m from the water surface.
Commence controlled flooding of buoyancy tanks BT-A2-1 and BT-A5-1 to 30%.

stages.name: Lift the hook to 47 m
actions: Lift the hook to a height of 47 m from the water surface.

stages.name: Flood legs L-B5-2 and L-B2-2
actions: Maintain the hook at 47 m from the water surface.
Commence free flooding of legs L-B5-2 and L-B2-2 to 100%.

stages.name: Flood legs L-B5-1, L-B2-1, L-C2-1 and L-C5-1
actions: Maintain the hook at 47 m from the water surface.
Commence free flooding of leg L-B5-1 to 100% and controlled flooding of legs L-B2-1 to 50%, L-C2-1 to 53% and L-C5-1 to 53%.

stages.name: Lower the hook to 43 m, 1 m above the seabed
actions: Lower the main hook to 43 m from the water surface.
The jacket is 1 m from the seabed, for ROV inspection.

stages.name: Lower the hook to 42 m, prepare for on-bottom
actions: Lower the main hook to 42 m from the water surface.

stages.name: On-bottom condition
actions: All jacket leg compartments are flooded up to water level; buoyancy tanks at rows A2, A5, C2, C5 and H0 are 100% flooded.
Open the drain caisson ABH-6204 (J-tube OD 273 x 12.7 WT) and the caissons ABH-4901A and ABH-4901B, flooded up to water level.
See the jacket on-bottom stability analysis and mudmat design report 2021-4589-6J-1017 for the minimum and maximum on-bottom weight.
